topic: A person finds out their surprise party has been cancelled
text: I reckoned the grain would be rich and golden, much like the one from last year that filled our barn to the brim. But now, the sky turns ashen, much like when the storm clouds brew over the hill. They say the party was to be a feast of mirth and joy, a fine distraction from the toil and furrow. I envisioned the comunidad gathering, the halls decked with greens, the hearths warming with laughter and cheer. But the word comes that it's to be cancelled. The crops, they cannot save this. The saints may understand, but the heart feels the weight of an empty hall, as if the earth has shifted, leaving us with nothing but the turn of the plow and the long, silent night.
